**This is a release candidate.** FontDaw 0.1.1 Public RC1 is a test version. It may still have
bugs; keep copies of scores you care about.

FontDaw is a fork of MuseScore Studio that adds audio tracks, recording and mixing around the score.

## About the warnings

None of the files are signed with a known developer ID (no Apple Developer ID, no Windows
code-signing certificate). So macOS (Gatekeeper) and Windows (SmartScreen) will flag them as coming
from an unidentified developer; that warning is expected. They should not trigger a virus or malware
warning. If your antivirus reports one, don't open the file; check the download against its
`.sha256` checksum and report it on the project's GitHub issues page.

## Check the download

Each file has a `.sha256` file next to it. Download both into the same folder, open a terminal
there, and run:

- macOS: `shasum -a 256 -c FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-macOS-arm64.dmg.sha256`. It must print "OK".
- Linux: `sha256sum -c FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-linux-x86_64.AppImage.sha256`. It must print "OK".
- Windows (PowerShell): `Get-FileHash .\FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`
  (or the `.msi`), then compare the hash it prints with the one in the `.sha256` file.

The checksum confirms that the file is the one this release's build made, and that it was not
changed on the way. You can also upload a file to an online scanner such as VirusTotal before
opening it.

## Your MuseScore files are safe

- FontDaw never overwrites a file that was saved by MuseScore 4 or later, or by a newer version of
  FontDaw. When you save such a file, FontDaw explains why and offers Save As, with " (FontDaw)"
  added to the name, so the copy goes next to the original. The original stays as it was.
- Files from MuseScore 3 or earlier are imported; save them under a new name.
- MuseScore does not open a file once FontDaw has saved it. To go back to MuseScore, use
  **File → Export…** in FontDaw, choose MusicXML, and open that file in MuseScore. That keeps the
  notes and most markings, but not audio tracks, mixer settings or plug-in settings.

## Installing

A platform that is missing from this release did not pass its build check this time.

### macOS (Apple silicon): `FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-macOS-arm64.dmg`

1. Open the `.dmg` file and drag FontDaw to Applications.
2. The app is not notarised by Apple, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 or later:
   - open FontDaw once; macOS refuses it;
   - go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down, click **Open Anyway** next to
     FontDaw, and confirm.

   Or, in Terminal, after the checksum matched:
   `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FontDaw.app`. This only removes the "downloaded
   from the internet" mark from this one app; use it only on a file whose checksum matched.

   On macOS 14 or earlier: right-click (or Control-click) FontDaw, choose **Open**, and confirm.
3. After that, FontDaw opens normally.

### Windows (64-bit): `FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-windows-x64.zip` or `….msi`

- The `.zip` needs no installation: unpack it and start `FontDaw.exe` in its `bin` folder. The
  `.msi`, when present, installs FontDaw like other programs.
- FontDaw is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time. Choose **More info →
  Run anyway**.
- This version has not yet been tested on a real Windows computer, only by its automatic build
  check.

### Linux (x86_64): `FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-linux-x86_64.AppImage`

- Make the file executable (`chmod +x FontDaw-0.1.1-Public-RC1-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, or tick
  "Allow executing file as program" in its properties), then run it.
- This version has been tested only by its automatic build check.
